notes.summary: Projects open in a popup and list their steps on To-do, steps run in the order you give them, and work isn't left unplanned when there's time.
new: A project, an exam or an ongoing project opens in a popup in the middle of the screen. Escape, the ✕ or a click outside closes it.
A project with steps shows on To-do as a heading over its steps, not as a to-do of its own; click the heading to open the project. A project with no steps is still a to-do, worked on as a whole.
Ticking a project's last step finishes the project too, and one Undo puts both back.
If you gave a project more time than its steps add up to, the rest is a step of its own, "More on <project>", kept up to date as you change the steps. Delete it and it stays gone.
A project's steps run in the order you list them, each after the one above it. Click "then" between two steps to make one "any time" instead. Reordering moves them at once.
A project's due date and how firm it is are set at the top of the project.
An exam's popup says what happens before an exam, "Only its class's work, 3 days before", and you can change it right there for all your exams.
Every page says "Replanning…" while Friday plans a change, then "Plan updated".
An event's color can be changed on its card.
If you're not in school, New project offers a report, a presentation and an event to plan.
changed: A project's pace (front-loaded, evenly or toward the end) now visibly changes when its work is planned.
A step planned past the next two weeks says when ("Later, by Wed 9 Dec") instead of "not planned".
Projects & exams lists only projects and exams; big assignments stay on To-do.
An ongoing project can have a tag.
"Focus on exams starting 5 days before" and similar wording are understood as exam focus.
A due date you pick is said as a sentence, "Due Tue 24 Nov, 11:59pm (in 7 days)".
Try elsewhere, when nothing else fits, says what rules the other times out.
Time you shoved says what it is on its card.
fixed: Work could be left unplanned, even with free time, when that time came only in short gaps (an ongoing project could get no time at all that week).
A daily repeat set to be spaced several days apart stopped Friday from planning.
A timer started before midnight shows on the previous day too.
Steps that all had lengths were told to "give them a length".
Steps with similar names were made to wait on each other.
A rule clash in the Inbox could say work moves "to 10:15am from 10:15am".
An event's location could run under a meal or a timer drawn over it.
Hints in typing boxes were cut off in a few places, and a Morning brief line on a phone.
The Now bar's timing dot was cut off on its left.
An overdue due date said "in -1 days"; it says "yesterday" or "3 days ago".
A rule clash could be reported when keeping the rule gained almost nothing.

notes.summary: A new Projects & exams page with ongoing projects, choices for events marked free, and lengths you can type.
new: Projects & exams is a new page: every deadline (projects, exams and big assignments) as a row across the next six weeks, your ongoing projects, and what you've finished. Everything you had before is on it.

Ongoing projects: hours a week with no deadline, like guitar or a side project. Choose how many days a week, its priority, a pause, and whether a short week carries into the next. Weekly goals you already had are listed there and plan as they always have until you change a setting.
A project can be archived when it's done, keep notes, finish a few days early, set its pace through the work (front-loaded, even or toward the end), and have milestones.
An exam opens beside the page, its prep a list you edit: rename, length, by when, tick, delete, or add more.
Events marked free in your calendar have the same choices as busy ones: I'm going, Work through it and Skip it. Work through it is chosen until you pick.
changed: A length (an exam's prep, a project or step, hours a week) offers common amounts and a box to type any, up to 1,000 hours.
Double-click a task's name in the To-do drawer to rename it.
Everything you're timing shows on the calendar while it runs, side by side.
Starting a nap while something is being timed asks whether to stop timing it.
The Now bar shows an event that takes your time before a free one that began earlier.
A pace set for a while says the day it ends in words: "Easy pace until tomorrow".
In the Inbox, the email a suggestion came from opens at the words Friday read.
fixed: Insights' hours map counts an hour once however many timers ran in it, and says it covers the weeks shown.
Two quick changes to the same thing are saved in the order you made them.
A dropdown's list is as wide as its button, not the whole window.
The Inbox's messages keep their height in a long list, and the plan's notice keeps its count on a phone.

notes.summary: A new version of Friday now asks as soon as it's out, dropdowns are never cut off, and the unfinished Rules lab is gone.
changed: Friday looks for a new version once a day and whenever you open its window, so a new release asks within a day instead of up to a month.
Later puts that version off until tomorrow; a newer version asks right away.
The Rules lab is gone. What worked from it is on the Rules page: Why?, "Violated on", editing a rule in place, and why two rules clash.
fixed: A dropdown's list is never cut off by the card or column it's in, like the tag menu on Projects & exams.
Closing the update popup no longer hides newer versions too.

notes.summary: All-day events and holidays come in from your calendars, rule clashes say why, the week can be lightened in a click, and the calendar turns over at midnight.
new: All-day events from your calendars, like holidays and your own all-day plans, show at the top of each day. One that reads like homework becomes a to-do due that day.
A rule clash says why, e.g. "finishing Lab 9 2 days sooner splits it into 3 sittings instead of 1". Only clashes where your answer would change the plan wait in the Inbox.
When a week or a day holds more than usual, "Lighten that week" offers work that can move later without being late, each tried first and undoable.
Change a project's or an exam's tag from its page or card. Its steps that had the old tag follow.
Remove a template you saved with the ✕ on its card, and saving one under a name you've used asks before replacing it.
A new exam takes any length: 45m to 3h in a click, or type one like 2h 30m.
changed: The calendar turns over at midnight: anything after midnight shows under the next date, and a block that crosses midnight shows in both days.
An event that doesn't block your time sits beside the work planned over it, not hidden behind it.
The two rules for meals and routines say what they're set to, like "Give meals and routines their ideal length: Lunch 45 min and Dinner 1 h".
Load ahead says it plainly: "16 h planned, 1 h past your usual 15 h. Nothing will be late."
The Minimal Now bar is a one-line pill; tap it for the full bar.
Text in a tall block wraps instead of being cut off.
A repeat says its spacing as a sentence: "Every week, at least 5 days after the last time".
"Final" marks an exam ("math final") for students, but not a final project, paper or round, or a name like Final Fantasy.
The Rules lab is hidden while it's unfinished; Settings → Advanced shows it again.
fixed: The Now bar no longer covers the Inbox's Accept and Decline (or any page's last buttons) when the sleep and meal rows are up.
"At least N days apart" now also spaces several times in the same week.
Save as template no longer keeps steps you deleted.
Load ahead no longer says a week is over your usual hours when it isn't: meals, goals and this morning's work were counted against it.
Rules no longer says a rule wins over one you've removed.
The day comparison runs from your day start, not midnight.
The Now bar's time no longer gets cut off in a narrow window.

notes.summary: Edit a rule where it stands and see why one wasn't kept, stop work for the night with one tap, choose which Reminders lists Friday plans, and see what's due in a row under each date.
new: Edit a rule instead of deleting it: the pencil opens it with your words. Saving keeps its place and history, and Undo puts it back.
A rule the plan couldn't keep says "Violated on Tue, Thu", and Why? says in plain words what needed those hours.
Exam focus is a rule now ("Focus on an exam's course 5 days before it"), listed in Rules with its switch and its days to change.
Exam prep is spread over the days before the exam by default, as a rule in Rules you can switch off or make stronger.
Apple Reminders: choose which of your lists come into Friday. A list you switch off leaves your plan at once and stays in Reminders.
A 24-hour clock, in Settings → Appearance → Clock: every page, Siri and the command line follow it.
A small spinner on an integration while Friday reads it for the first time, and reads now start within a second.
changed: After "Done with work", nothing more is planned that night. What then can't be done on time waits in the Inbox.
A calendar you hid is ignored everywhere: its invitations no longer come to the Inbox.
The sleep buttons show when you need them: Done with work from 6pm, Going to bed right after it, and I'm up after any night you went to bed.
An optional early event you haven't said you're going to no longer wakes you early.
Tasks are no longer marked spread or clustered. Say it as a rule instead, like "spread my essays over several days".
The Rules box has no row of examples under it.
The to-do lane is a row under each day's date with what's due that day: late ones first, three and "+N more" for the rest. The hours below keep their full width.
The Setup walk's times are in a clearer pixel font: 6:15 no longer reads as 6:18, nor 12am as 18am.
A project's step says which project it's in, on its card and in the to-do list, and opens it.
Colors are listed in rainbow order, gray last.
Friday is written in US English: color, gray.
fixed: Going to bed at 4am or later counts as the night before, so the morning after pairs with it.
The red line for now shows at night and before you wake, not only during your day.
Plans no longer leave a long empty gap late at night between pieces of work, and replanning can improve the plan you have.
Text stays inside its box across the app, the calendars table fits its panel, and the "Read events as" menus are smaller.
A project whose steps are planned is no longer said to be unplanned, and once its steps are done its own time isn't planned.
A rule's hours before or after a time run to the start of your day, not 4am.
Stopping and restarting a repeat keeps the times you removed one by one.
Removing a source and forgetting it keeps the suggestions you'd accepted from it.
Work due at midnight on a Saturday isn't planned a week late.
Meals and naps across a clock change keep their times and lengths.
Signing in to Slack, Microsoft and others no longer runs out when two parts of Friday renew it at once.
A Shortcut that adds "Tom & Jerry" adds all of it, & and # included.
The mini calendar follows the calendar, and the View buttons keep the day you're looking at.
The paint menu closes with Esc, and an integration's box keeps the keyboard inside it.
What if and other slower questions no longer hold up the rest of the page.
Setup's day bars keep their times inside the box, and "fits" no longer reads as "Ats".

notes.summary: Friday plans the to-dos from the apps you already use, asks what you'll do in an event's time, and every click answers at once.
new: Todoist, TickTick, Notion, Trello, Apple Reminders, Things and Google Tasks: their to-dos are planned into your week, and ticking one off in either place ticks it off in both.
Asana, Linear, Jira and GitHub: work assigned to you is planned in. Canvas's own assignments, and Slack messages that mention you.
More calendar links from school and work, each with its steps: Blackboard, Moodle, Brightspace, Schoology, Homebase, When I Work, Deputy, 7shifts and Sling.
Mail from iCloud, Yahoo, Fastmail or any other provider, with an app password, beside Gmail.
Your plan as a "Friday" calendar in iCloud, so your iPhone shows it.
An event's card asks what you'll do: go, work through it (Friday plans work in its time), or skip it.
The first time Friday opens, a short tour shows each page and what it's for; afterwards the ? numbers the buttons on the page you're on and lists what each does.
friday:// links for Shortcuts: add a to-do or open a page.
changed: Clicks answer at once: Inbox answers, timers and the length steppers no longer wait for Friday to finish saving.
Notes about you are on the Rules page, beside your rules: type one and press Keep as a note.
A block's card stays open after what you do in it, showing what changed.
Each integration opens in a box of its own, closed with × or Esc.
Settings says less, and more plainly.
fixed: The Inbox no longer freezes when it opens before Friday has finished loading.
Enter in search, with nothing found, adds what you typed as a to-do.
A project's step shows what it waits on.
The weekly review offers Next week only for work due after next Monday.
A task due at midnight repeats on the right days.
What changed opens after you undo an add.
⌘-clicking a second block picks the one you'd selected too.
Change a Setup answer opens the question you picked.
"today" typed after midnight means the same day as the Today button.
The to-do list's done section is called Done.
Double clicks no longer make two exams, projects, steps or to-dos, or send a review twice.
One integration that can't be read no longer stops the others from syncing.
Friday left open overnight moves on to the new day by itself.
The Mac app starts Friday again if it stops by itself, and no longer keeps the processor busy after it stops.
An event moved by an hour in Calendar or Reminders is synced at once, not up to an hour later.
Work due at exactly the start of a day is planned the day before.
Renaming a tag keeps the rules that name it.
Forgetting one mailbox no longer switches off another whose address ends the same.

notes.summary: Connecting Gmail is right in Setup, and Settings no longer makes Google look calendar-only.
new: Setup lists Gmail beside your calendars: make an app password, paste it with your address, done.
changed: Settings → Integrations keeps the advanced Google option (your own Google Cloud key) closed, and says most people don't need it.
fixed: Connecting Gmail with an app password no longer opens the Google Cloud key-file steps.

notes.summary: Google works for everyone through your Mac, Friday's questions wait in your Inbox, new terms to accept, and fixes for timers, time steppers and calendar edge cases.
new: Friday's terms: everyone accepts them when Friday opens, and again whenever they change.

Friday's questions now wait in your Inbox: what it learned, which version of a day you'd rather have, your meal times and your bedtimes. "Not now" asks again once Friday knows more; Insights links there.
When something from your mail updates a task you have, the card says what will change.
changed: Google comes in through your Mac: add your Google account in System Settings → Internet Accounts for its calendars, and read Gmail with an app password. Signing in to Google directly, which Google blocked for most people, is now only for someone with a Google Cloud key of their own (Settings → Integrations → Advanced).
Friday's code is under the PolyForm Noncommercial License.
fixed: "Forgot to stop?" starts at the time it is now, not 9am, and its buttons line up.
Tapping − and + quickly, or going back after overshooting, keeps the length you see.
Updating a task from your Inbox keeps the name you gave it.
A 2:30am event on the night the clocks go forward is no longer refused.
Changing your timezone keeps all-day events on their days.
An event made all-day in Google while all-day events are off leaves Friday.
Undoing a delete, or opening a deleted event again, puts it back on its calendar.
Work can't be logged before it has happened.
Security updates for the parts Friday is built with.

notes.summary: Repeats you make work as they should, any Gmail with an app password, colors for events from the start, Friday on your phone, and many fixes from a full check of the app.
new: Friday on your phone over Tailscale: pair it with a QR code in Settings → Phone.
Read any Gmail with an app password, in Settings → Integrations → Gmail.
Events get colors from the start: Exam, Class, Meeting, Work, Exercise, Social and Travel, all yours to change.
The calendars on your Mac lead Settings → Integrations, and you can change one Setup answer without going through Setup again.
Keep a repeating task's times apart: "laundry at least 7 days apart".
A built-in preference to stay on one course for a stretch, and a switch for doing things in one go (Settings → Schedule).
A sentence with several times, like "no work 7:10–7:20 and 7:30–7:40", adds a rule for each; under any rule Friday read itself, "Not what you meant?" asks your AI.
"If math homework becomes overdue, it must be done before Sunday" is read as a rule.
changed: Sleep and Meals are tabs of Insights.
Errors say what happened and what to do, in plain words.
The intro's town matches the season outside.
Double-clicking a planned task opens it in your to-dos.
Many more rules are read without the AI, and one Friday only half understands goes to the AI instead of being guessed.
fixed: Events you make in Friday repeat as they should.
Switching off a repeat that came from Google no longer deletes it from Google.
Canvas and other calendar-link repeats with an end date come in, once, and aren't copied into Google.
Free/busy and all-day changes made in Google reach Friday.
Quick add reads "due 5pm fri", page ranges and times after midnight as meant, and exam prep by its title.
Work you've already timed today counts toward your daily limit; changing a task's length changes what's planned.
Security: other websites and connected assistants can no longer reach your AI key or your private settings.
Security updates for Google sign-in.

notes.summary: Friday now lives at friday-scheduler.com, asks you less about your day, and gets birthdays and all-day events right.
new: Friday's site is friday-scheduler.com: the download, the Terminal install and updates all come from there, and downloads come from servers near you, so they're quicker.
changed: With "Plan it again" on (Settings → Schedule), Friday no longer asks how much you did of work you didn't time: it already knows.
A timer stopped in under five minutes doesn't count as work: Friday says it was too short to count and keeps the task to do.
A new all-day event, like a birthday, leaves the day free for planning unless you say otherwise.
fixed: Asking the AI to add a list of birthdays puts each one on the right day, whichever AI you use, and doesn't add one you already have.
Changing a repeating event from today on keeps its next date: yearly birthdays no longer all moved to today.
Deleting a repeating event from one time on removes those times from your calendar too.

notes.summary: Friday now updates itself, asking you first and saying what changed.
new: When a new version is out, Friday asks the next time it opens, with what's new in it.
Update downloads it while you keep working, checks it's the version Friday's site published, and restarts into it.
The first time a new version opens, Friday shows what changed.
Settings → Updates: the version you have, Check now, and whether an update goes in right away or when you quit.

notes.summary: The first version of Friday you can download.
new: Plans your week: tasks planned into your free time before they’re due, around your classes, work, meals and sleep, and planned again when things change.
Walk through your week: a first run through a pixel-art town that sets Friday up from your answers.
One list: everything you have to do by kind, with its time, when it’s planned and when it’s due.
Your Mac’s calendars and calendar feeds come in; events you make can go back to your calendar.
The Inbox, the review and rules in your own words: Friday asks only what it can’t know.
Ask the AI you choose, or none.
Everything runs on your Mac: no account, nothing to install besides the app.
